output.title: Greeting for a Medicare Advantage (MA) pharmacy education call
output.draft_text:
Use this greeting when you answer a Medicare Advantage (MA) pharmacy education call. Say it in your own words and keep it short (see U-RX-EDU-001-01).

1. Open the call. Greet the caller and give your name and [plan or department name to state, for example the approved MA plan or pharmacy team name]. Example structure: "Thank you for calling [plan or department name]. My name is [advocate first name]. How can I help you today?" Replace this with the approved wording once it is confirmed.

2. Give any required statements. [Required opening disclosures for MA pharmacy calls, for example call recording notice or other required statements, if any, and their exact wording.]

3. Verify the caller. Verify the caller using [required verification elements, for example the identifiers to request and how many must match]. If you cannot verify the caller, offer to call the member back (see U-RX-EDU-001-06).

4. Confirm what the IVR captured. If the IVR already captured the drug name, do not ask the member to retell the whole story. Confirm the drug and the pharmacy, then move on (see U-RX-EDU-001-03). If the IVR did not capture the drug name, [steps to follow when no drug name was captured].

5. Move to education. Move into the pharmacy education topic. [Any required transition statement or the order of steps after the greeting.]
placeholders: [plan or department name to state, for example the approved MA plan or pharmacy team name]
[Required opening disclosures for MA pharmacy calls, for example call recording notice or other required statements, if any, and their exact wording.]
[required verification elements, for example the identifiers to request and how many must match]
[steps to follow when no drug name was captured]
[Any required transition statement or the order of steps after the greeting.]
author_checklist: Decide whether a scripted greeting is required for MA pharmacy education calls, or whether advocates may use their own words as U-RX-EDU-001-01 says. Then align this unit with that decision.
Confirm the exact plan or department name advocates should state when they open the call.
Confirm whether advocates must give their first name, full name, or an ID.
Confirm with Compliance or Legal whether any required opening statements apply to MA pharmacy calls, such as a call recording notice, and get their exact wording.
Confirm the verification elements required before discussing member pharmacy information.
Confirm the process when the IVR did not capture a drug name.
Confirm whether a required transition statement or step order applies after the greeting.
Remove or replace the example greeting structure once the approved wording is confirmed.
Check that this unit does not duplicate or conflict with U-RX-EDU-001-01, -03, and -06, and decide whether it should be numbered in the U-RX-EDU-001 series (for example as -02).
